20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机

42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

1	Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a fully crossed design with up to seven facets across open-weight instruction-tuned models and five benchmarks. Under binary correctness scoring, a recommended 3-prompt $\times$ 3-seed design achieves $G \geq 0.80$ with 178 items---a 3.1$\times$ item reduction over single-condition designs at the cost of 2.9$\times$ more total evaluations---a tradeoff that favors multi-facet designs when item construction is costly. Variance decomposition reveals that models differ primarily in which items they find difficult rather than in overall ability, and that the variance structure shifts qualitatively between multiple-choice and free-form benchmarks. Preliminary validation across model scales and architecture families confirms structural stability. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and decision-study (D-study) budget calculator for evaluation design optimization\footnote{Code and data are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/nlp_variance_gtheory-11E1/}.}.

tool_args.content: Large Language Model (LLM) benchmark results shift with prompt phrasing, random seeds, and item selection, yet no unified framework determines which source matters most or how sources interact across evaluation settings. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory), a psychometric framework for multi-facet variance decomposition, in a factorial design crossing seven evaluation facets across eight models and five benchmarks. The resulting variance structure is format-conditional: on multiple-choice benchmarks, item-related factors account for over two-thirds of total variance, while on free-form reasoning benchmarks variance disperses across items, models, and prompts with no single dominant source. Models differ primarily in which items they find difficult, not in overall ability. This asymmetry carries a practical consequence: evaluation designs that average over multiple prompts and seeds require an order of magnitude fewer test items for reliable measurement than single-condition designs. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and Decision-study (D-study) budget calculator for evaluation design optimization\footnote{Code and data are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/nlp_variance_gtheory-11E1/}.}.
